drivingQuestion: Which verse teaches that one praises God for the bad exactly as for the good?
outcomeNote: Four alternative prooftexts are set out for the same rule and none is rejected or preferred; the unit then turns to the maxim that all God does is for the good and illustrates it with the story of Rabbi Akiva on the road.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אַחָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי לֵוִי: מַאי קְרָא — ״חֶסֶד וּמִשְׁפָּט אָשִׁירָה לְךָ ה׳ אֲזַמֵּרָה״. אִם חֶסֶד — אָשִׁירָה, וְאִם מִשְׁפָּט — אָשִׁירָה.
segments.en: «Rav Aḥa said in the name of Rabbi Levi: What» is the «verse» that alludes to this? «“I will sing of loving-kindness and justice; unto You, O Lord, will I sing praises”» (Psalms 101:1). Rav Aḥa explains: «If» it is «loving-kindness, I will sing, and if» it is «justice, I will sing.» I will thank God in song for the bad just as for the good.

segments.he: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר, מֵהָכָא: ״בַּה׳ אֲהַלֵּל דָּבָר בֵּאלֹהִים אֲהַלֵּל דָּבָר״. בַּה׳ אֲהַלֵּל דָּבָר — זוֹ מִדָּה טוֹבָה, בֵּאלֹהִים אֲהַלֵּל דָּבָר — זוֹ מִדַּת פּוּרְעָנוּת.
segments.en: «Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:» The proof is «from here,» as it is stated: «“In God, I will praise His word; in the Lord, I will praise His word”» (Psalms 56:11). The Gemara explains that «In God, I will praise His word; that is» the revelation of God’s «attribute of benevolence,» while: «In the Lord, I will praise His word; that is the attribute of suffering;» even if God brings suffering to bear upon me, I will still praise Him.

segments.he: רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר: מֵהָכָא: ״כּוֹס יְשׁוּעוֹת אֶשָּׂא וּבְשֵׁם ה׳ אֶקְרָא״, ״צָרָה וְיָגוֹן אֶמְצָא וּבְשֵׁם ה׳ אֶקְרָא״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Tanḥum said:» The proof is «from here,» as it is stated: «“I will lift up the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord”» (Psalms 116:13), and: «“I found trouble and sorrow, but I called upon the name of the Lord”» (Psalms 116:3–4).

segments.he: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי, מֵהָכָא: ״ה׳ נָתָן וַה׳ לָקָח יְהִי שֵׁם ה׳ מְבֹרָךְ״.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis said:» The proof is «from here,» as it is stated: «“The Lord has given and the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord”» (Job 1:21).

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְכֵן תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם רָגִיל לוֹמַר: ״כׇּל דְּעָבֵיד רַחֲמָנָא לְטָב עָבֵיד״.
segments.en: «Rav Huna said» that «Rav said» that «Rabbi Meir said; and so it was taught» in a baraita «in the name of Rabbi Akiva: One must always accustom oneself to say: Everything that God does, He does for the best.»

segments.he: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דַּהֲוָה קָאָזֵיל בְּאוֹרְחָא. מְטָא לְהַהִיא מָתָא, בְּעָא אוּשְׁפִּיזָא לָא יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ. אֲמַר: ״כׇּל דְּעָבֵיד רַחֲמָנָא — לְטָב״. אֲזַל וּבָת בְּדַבְרָא, וַהֲוָה בַּהֲדֵיהּ תַּרְנְגוֹלָא וַחֲמָרָא וּשְׁרָגָא. אֲתָא זִיקָא כַּבְיֵיהּ לִשְׁרָגָא. אֲתָא שׁוּנָּרָא אַכְלֵיהּ לְתַרְנְגוֹלָא. אֲתָא אַרְיָה אַכְלֵיהּ לַחֲמָרָא. אֲמַר: ״כׇּל דְּעָבֵיד רַחֲמָנָא — לְטָב״. בֵּיהּ בְּלֵילְיָא אֲתָא גְּיָיסָא, שַׁבְיַיהּ לְמָתָא. אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָאו אֲמַרִי לְכוּ כׇּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹשֶׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «Like this» incident, «when Rabbi Akiva was walking along the road and came to a certain city, he inquired about lodging and they did not give him» any. «He said: Everything that God does, He does for the best. He went and slept in a field, and he had with him a rooster, a donkey and a candle. A» gust of «wind came and extinguished the candle; a cat came and ate the rooster; and a lion came and ate the donkey. He said: Everything that God does, He does for the best. That night, an army came and took the city into captivity.» It turned out that Rabbi Akiva alone, who was not in the city and had no lit candle, noisy rooster or donkey to give away his location, was saved. «He said to them: Didn’t I tell you? Everything that God does,»

moves.summary: a third verse: the cup of salvation and trouble and sorrow both bring calling on the Name
moves.about: the cup of salvation over which the name of the Lord is called

moves.summary: a fourth verse: Job blesses the Name for the giving and for the taking
moves.about: Job blessing the Name for what was given and what was taken

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא אמר רב משום רבי מאיר
moves.summary: a tradent chain reaching Rabbi Meir, and a baraita in Rabbi Akiva's name: always say that all the Merciful One does is for the good
moves.about: the maxim that all the Merciful One does is for the good

moves.cueHe: כי הא דרבי עקיבא דהוה קאזיל באורחא
moves.summary: the story of the refused lodging, the extinguished candle and the eaten rooster and donkey, and the troop that took the city that night
moves.about: the night Rabbi Akiva was refused lodging, lost candle, rooster and donkey, and was thereby saved from the raiding troop

moves.summary: the close of Rabbi Akiva's words to the townspeople: it is all for the good
moves.about: having been saved by the very losses of that night, he tells the townspeople that this bears out what he had said
